stories.title: Berlin provides zero evidence of Russian involvement in Leipzig incident — ambassador
stories.summary: The Russian Embassy in Berlin earlier described the incident as a hastily fabricated provocation
article_sentences: BERLIN, September 2.
Russian Ambassador to Germany Sergey Nechaev said that Berlin has no material evidence of Russia’s involvement in last month's drone incident at Leipzig/Halle Airport.
"We are being accused of no less than committing a terrorist act or attempting to do so," Nechaev told Russian journalists.
"Some testimony, material evidence and professional assessments - in short, a solid case - should support such serious accusations.
There is none.
Therefore, all this is perplexing to say the very least," the diplomat said.
He noted that Russia has friendly relations with the federal state of Saxony and the city of Leipzig.
Nechaev also recalled that Russian President Vladimir Putin had stressed that there was no evidence of Russia’s involvement.
"We, for our part, can say that none of this has been presented to us.
If you have found something, fine.
Organize a meeting of specialists and experts, including Russian ones," the ambassador said.
A thorough investigation, he said, could clearly and simply demonstrate that the incident had nothing to do with intelligence activities.

stories.title: Woman charged with juror intimidation in Lindsay Clancy trial
stories.summary: A woman, who was arrested for taking photos of jury members outside the courthouse in the Lindsay Clancy trial, has been charged with aggravated intimidation of a juror. Dawn Light, 56, is accused of sitting in a restricted area outside the Plymouth courthouse and photographing jurors as they exited the building on Tuesday. Her lawyer called it a misunderstanding as she pleaded not guilty to the charges. Lindsay Clancy, 36, is charged with the murders of her three children. The livestreamed trial has captured national and international media attention, and drawn strong, often deeply divided reactions from audiences. The jury has been deliberating on the case since Thursday. During Dawn Light's appearance in the court on Wednesday, Massachusetts lawyers said the sanctity of the judicial system was at risk because of her actions. Light, a registered nurse with no prior criminal record, was ordered to stay away from the courthouse grounds and also from those associated with the Clancy trial. She was also ordered not to produce or disseminate photos that could have been preserved on iCloud. Prosecutors requested a $50,000 (£37,000) cash bail, which was denied by the judge. "This is a complete misunderstanding your honor. my client was trying to get a picture of Ms Clancy," Light's attorney Jennifer White said in court.
